## The Leap to Urban Splendour

The cities of the **Sindhu-Sarasvatī Civilisation** did not appear overnight.

At Pre-Harappan sites like **Bhirrana** and **Kunal** in Haryana (dating back to 7000-5500 BCE), communities had already developed distinctive painted pottery, terracotta figurines, and bead-making industries.

By 2600 BCE, these regional cultures unified into a mature urban civilisation stretching over 1.5 million square kilometres.

**Harappan engineers planned their cities on a strict orthogonal grid, dividing settlements into a fortified western Citadel and an expansive Lower Town.**
